rationale_evidence.anchor: EKS has no runtime. It has mechanisms. There is no EKS service, daemon, scheduler, queue, database, or deployment unit. Every EKS behaviour is a command-line program that a human or an AI process chooses to invoke, plus a set of files in the repository.
rationale_evidence.statement: Single most important structural finding of the baseline: EKS has no runtime, only mechanisms -- no service, daemon, scheduler, queue, database, or deployment unit exists; every EKS behaviour is a CLI program invoked by a human or AI process plus a set of repository files, and nothing in EKS runs unless something outside it runs it.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The two EKS subsystems have inverse operational vitality, and the more valuable one is the less durable one. ... The subsystem that carries authority, ownership, and lineage for every governed engineering act writes to an untracked local directory. The subsystem that carries advisory code metrics writes to git.
rationale_evidence.statement: Third major finding, first-hand and not stated in any prior document: the Governance/Workflow subsystem (last active 2026-08-21, gitignored, 29 tests, no CI gate) and the Observation/Assurance subsystem (last active 2026-08-04, git-tracked, 43+252 tests, one non-blocking CI gate) have inverse operational vitality -- the subsystem carrying authority/ownership/lineage is untracked, while the subsystem carrying advisory metrics is durably persisted.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Answer to the joining-architect test ... Yes for the mechanisms, No for the domain. ... EKS's conceptual model is more mature than its executable boundaries, and its executable mechanisms are more mature than its domain model. Both statements are true simultaneously
rationale_evidence.statement: Summary verdict of the whole baseline: a joining Principal Architect could understand EKS's mechanisms (sections 8-11, 15-16) precisely enough to run and extend them, but not its domain (sections 6-7, 9 show unmodelled language, unassigned invariant ownership, and only-candidate boundaries) -- 'EKS's conceptual model is more mature than its executable boundaries, and its executable mechanisms are more mature than its domain model,' both true simultaneously.
